newsitem.title: UK: Cocoa slides, base metals consolidate.
newsitem.headline: Cocoa slides, base metals consolidate.

text.p: Cocoa prices extended a slide on Thursday, touching 18-month lows after a big sell-off on Wednesday when speculators decided to quit the market.

Funds, put off by a gloomy picture on the charts, raided the market again with aggressive sales on Thursday, driving London May cocoa futures to 871 pounds sterling as they dumped long positions and increased shorts.
The contract fell some five percent in value on Wednesday and closed six sterling down at 873.00 a tonne on Thursday.
In base metals, copper consolidated recent gains, going above $2,250 per tonne on the London Metal Exchange, but was unable to climb back to overnight peaks around $2,270 a tonne.
Three months delivery ended around $2,259.50 a tonne.
Zinc also consolidated gains from Wednesday, when it achieved a fresh two-year high of $1,190, to close steady at $1,180 a tonne.
The zinc market is seen as having further strength and should soon be ready to challenge the psychological $1,200 area and the January 1995 high of $1,239 a tonne, analysts said.
Elsewhere in commodities gold hovered around Wednesday levels to close barely unchanged at $343.30 an ounce, but still in danger of edging towards fresh 3-1/4 year lows around the $340.00 level.
London Robusta grade coffee saw modest losses amid light dealing, hovering around Wednesday levels at $1,555 a tonne.
Some leading commodity prices at 1730 GMT -
